zakat-calculator.assumptionNote: Zakat rules vary between schools of thought and scholars. This calculator uses the widely applied 2.5% on net zakatable wealth above nisab held for one lunar year. When in doubt, consult a scholar you trust.

faqs.a: Nisab is the minimum wealth threshold above which Zakat becomes due: 87.48 grams of gold or 612.36 grams of silver. Many scholars recommend using the silver nisab (the lower value), which makes more people eligible and is the default in this calculator - update it with the current silver price in your currency.

Yes. Gold jewellery is zakatable at its current market value, regardless of whether it is worn daily. Personal-use items like your home, car, and clothing are exempt. Enter the resale value of your gold in the gold field above.

Subtract short-term debts that are due within the year. Long-term debts like a 25-year mortgage are treated differently by different scholars: some deduct only the next 12 months of payments, others deduct nothing from zakatable wealth. This calculator subtracts whatever debt figure you enter, so follow your scholar's guidance.

Zakat is due on wealth held for one lunar year (hawl). In practice, most people pick a Zakat date (often in Ramadan) and pay on whatever they hold that day. If you received new money mid-year, many scholars allow paying on the full amount at your Zakat date for simplicity.
faqs.q: What if I held the money for less than a year?

faqs.a: Shares and funds are zakatable at their market value. If the company holds significant non-zakatable assets, some scholars allow deducting a portion - ask a scholar for your specific holdings. Business stock is valued at current wholesale price.
faqs.q: Are shares and mutual funds zakatable?

faqs.a: Zakat al-Mal (2.5% on wealth) is the annual obligation this calculator covers. Zakat al-Fitr is a separate fixed amount paid before Eid al-Fitr for every household member - it is not a percentage of wealth.
faqs.q: Zakat al-Mal vs Zakat al-Fitr - what is the difference?

zakat-calculator.formula:
Net zakatable wealth = cash + gold + silver + investments + business stock - debts.
If net wealth >= nisab: Zakat = net wealth x 2.5 / 100.
If net wealth < nisab: no Zakat due.
Example: 16,200 x 2.5 / 100 = 405.
howTo: Enter the current market value of your cash, bank balances, gold, and silver.
Add the market value of shares, funds, and any business stock.
Enter debts due within the year.
Set the nisab value in your currency (silver nisab is the cautious default).
Your Zakat due appears instantly - pay it to eligible recipients with a clear intention.
keyFacts: Zakat is 2.5% of net zakatable wealth held for one lunar year, one of the Five Pillars of Islam.
Nisab: 87.48g of gold or 612.36g of silver; below nisab, no Zakat is due.
Zakatable assets: cash, gold, silver, shares, business stock, and money owed to you.
Not zakatable: your home, car, furniture, and personal items you use.
Debts due within the year are subtracted before calculating.
The silver nisab is lower, so more people qualify - most scholars recommend using it.

zakat-calculator.quickAnswer: Zakat is 2.5% of your net zakatable wealth above nisab. With $5,000 cash, $3,000 gold, $200 silver, $10,000 investments, and $2,000 debts: net wealth is $16,200, so Zakat due is $405. If your net wealth is below nisab (about the value of 612g of silver), no Zakat is due.
zakat-calculator.tagline: Work out 2.5% Zakat on cash, gold, silver, and investments - with nisab check.
zakat-calculator.workedExample:
Cash $5,000, gold $3,000, silver $200, investments $10,000, debts $2,000:
1. Total assets = 5,000 + 3,000 + 200 + 10,000 = $18,200.
2. Net wealth = 18,200 - 2,000 = $16,200.
3. Compare with nisab ($560 silver nisab): 16,200 > 560, so Zakat is due.
4. Zakat = 16,200 x 2.5 / 100 = $405.
